title: NAFEMS R0027 Test 7 pressurized-cylinder secondary creep
purpose: Verify the native axisymmetric global implicit creep procedure against a public structure-level equilibrium and stress-redistribution benchmark, including spatial convergence and time-integration acceptance evidence.
physics: Plane-strain thick cylinder under constant internal pressure with Mises secondary power-law creep

source.organization: NAFEMS; publicly reproduced by Dassault Systemes SIMULIA
source.title: Test 7: Axisymmetric - pressurized cylinder, secondary creep

execution.evidence: The structural route applies the elastic pressure preload, advances 1000 hours with an endpoint creep-rate error estimate, and compares raw integration-point stresses with full-revolution volume-weighted relative L2 norms. Native Q2 axisymmetric meridians with one, two, and four radial cells produced maximum component errors of 1.40%, 0.203%, and 0.0268%, respectively. On the four-cell mesh the radial, hoop, and axial errors were 0.0141%, 0.0145%, and 0.0268%; 224 increments were accepted and every accepted endpoint-rate estimate satisfied 5e-4. The older 3D quarter-sector route remains available as an explicit comparison formulation rather than defining the public benchmark.

observables: Radial, hoop and axial stress versus physical radius.
Accepted and rejected physical-time increments and endpoint creep-rate error estimates.
Final global residual norm and wall equilibrium.
acceptance: The dependency-free analytical oracle reproduces the published five-radius stress table.
The four-cell structural result must keep radial, hoop and axial full-revolution volume-weighted integration-point errors below 0.5 percent.
One-, two-, and four-cell Q2 meridians must show monotone spatial convergence for all three stress components.
Every accepted increment must satisfy the declared endpoint creep-rate integration estimate, independently of Newton convergence.
The elastic pressure preload and subsequent held-pressure creep step remain separate scientific procedures.
The four-cell structural calculation is an automated focused test; the dependency-free analytical oracle remains in regular CI.
limitations: The public Abaqus deck uses four CAX8R radial elements and at most 40 increments. AgentFEM uses a native Q2 axisymmetric meridian and currently accepts 224 increments under its independent endpoint-rate controller; stress accuracy is verified, but execution efficiency is not claimed equivalent.
The 0.5 percent component criterion is an AgentFEM verification contract, not an official NAFEMS acceptance tolerance.

The public Abaqus comparison reports differences rather than an acceptance limit: the largest tabulated radial-stress difference is 1.84 percent for CAX8R (1.85 percent for CCL24R), and the largest hoop-stress difference is 1.00 percent.
Two endpoint-rate tolerances provide a terminal-time refinement check; richer transient-history convergence remains a separate obligation when intermediate-time response is used.
